item.title: Mishima-machi Kouji Pickles: A Fermented Mountain Craft — Guide
item.description: Mishima-machi, a small mountain village in the Aizu region, is known for kouji-zuke — vegetables pickled and fermented using rice kouji (the mould culture also used in sake and miso production), a preservation tradition passed down through generations of local households to survive the region’s long, snowbound winters. The result is a mildly sweet, umami-rich pickle distinct from vinegar-based tsukemono, sold at farm stands, local markets and specialty shops throughout the village.
